channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Gold Holds Decline as US Jobs Data Fan December Rate Hike Bets
item.description: Gold held a late-week retreat after strong US jobs data reinforced expectations the Federal Reserve will seek to raise interest rates to combat inflation.
item.dc:creator: Wendy Wells

item.title: Nvidia Probes Huang Affair Amid Spying Controversy
item.description: Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang says he is cooperating fully with an independent board investigation after admitting to an extramarital relationship. The inquiry follows US intelligence suspicions that a female executive was recruited by a Chinese intelligence agency. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Nov. 9
item.description: Oil extended its biggest weekly loss since April 2020 as traders weighed diplomatic efforts to end the US-Iran conflict against fresh attacks in the region.
item.dc:creator: Kanoko Matsuyama

item.title: Australia Regulator Halts Private Credit Fund on Bathla Risks
item.description: Australia’s regulator stopped Angas Securities Ltd. from selling two managed investment schemes, the latest in a slew of actions to prevent private credit funds offering products that don’t adequately highlight potential risks.
item.dc:creator: Adam Haigh

item.title: Asian Stocks to Open Higher, Nvidia Probe Looms: Markets Wrap
item.description: Asian stocks looked set for advances early Monday as traders weighed gains in US equities against fresh uncertainty surrounding Nvidia Corp.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Burgess

item.title: New Zealand Dollar Advances as Ruling Party Gets Election Edge
item.description: New Zealand’s dollar edged higher in early trading after the incumbent National Party emerged from the weekend election with a path back to power, putting it in pole position to lead negotiations with minor parties.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Burgess

item.title: Treasury Rally Gets New Boost as Election Hammers the AI Trade
item.description: Wall Street sees the Treasury market emerging as a winner from the Democratic landslide in the US midterm elections, giving traders another reason to rethink this year’s sharp selloff.
item.dc:creator: Michael MacKenzie and Ye Xie

item.title: Watching Wall Street, Deadly Mass Shooting in Poland, Back to Work After Blue Wave
item.description: The news doesn’t stop when markets close. Hosts David Gura, Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo bring clarity, context and a bit of humor to the weekend’s biggest headlines, LIVE from New York. Joined by Fmr. Deputy Secretary of State & Fmr. US Special Representative for North Korea Stephen Biegun, SMBC Nikko Securities Chief Economist Joe Lavorgna, Author & Journalist Hannah Howard, North Carolina Rep Elect Paul Barringer, Virginia Rep Elect Shannon Taylor, Rising Communications President Leslie Shedd and Causeway Strategy Group Principal John McCarthy. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bookmarked: News Stories On Our Reading List
item.description: The Met Gala announces a 'normie' theme, the end of floppy disks, lawsuit over McRib contents, and the Hall of Fame of Toys: Join hosts David Gura, Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo on Bloomberg This Weekend for Bookmarked, where they share stories that caught their attention over the past week. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: By The Way: Headlines You May Have Missed
item.description: Choosing who to give Christmas presents to, a Christmas themed cruise, students making a deposit for college and then not attending, and the SATs and AP tests tackle AI cheating: Join Lisa Mateo, David Gura and Christina Ruffini for a roundup of headlines you may have missed, but gotta see. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Markets Brace for Washington Policy Battles
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, SMBC Nikko Securities Chief Economist Joe Lavorgna says affordability helped drive the midterm results but argues the underlying US economy remains healthy and major policy changes may be limited by divided government. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Lavorgna discusses the outlook for AI investment, inflation and markets as Washington prepares for two years of potential policy. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Israel’s Election Fight Shifts to Coalition Building
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg Middle East reporter Dan Williams explains why Gadi Eisenkot has been given the first opportunity to form Israel’s next government despite Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc winning more seats. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Williams discusses the role of Arab parties in coalition negotiations, Netanyahu’s political future and what could happen if Eisenkot fails to assemble a majority. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Can Europe Afford Its Welfare State?
item.description: Europe’s postwar welfare state was built for a younger, growing population. Today, aging communities are putting pensions, health care and public finances under mounting strain. As governments try to fund defense, infrastructure and education at the same time, the fight over who pays is spilling into politics and the streets. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: New House Democrats Set Their Priorities
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Democratic Reps.-elect Paul Barringer of North Carolina and Shannon Taylor of Virginia say voters sent them to Washington with a mandate to address affordability, health care and government accountability. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, they discuss working across the aisle, restoring congressional authority and responding to concerns about tariffs, data centers and the cost of living. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Luxury Gyms Turn Fitness Into a Family Affair
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg Pursuits writer Hannah Howard explains how high end fitness clubs are courting families with everything from child care and swimming lessons to homework help and activities for older kids. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Howard discusses why parents are willing to pay hundreds or even more than $1,000 a month for clubs that combine workouts, activities and family time under one roof. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Seattle and Las Vegas Make Their NBA Pitch
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg senior sports reporter Randall Williams explains why the NBA’s potential expansion to Seattle and Las Vegas could generate billions of dollars while raising questions about the financial returns for existing owners. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Williams also examines the competition among prospective ownership groups, LIV Golf’s struggles and the labor battle threatening Major League Baseball’s next season. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ukraine Peace Push Returns to Abu Dhabi
item.description: US, Ukrainian and Russian delegations are scheduled to meet in Abu Dhabi on November 10th and 11th, with Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner expected to represent the US. Joining Bloomberg This Weekend former Deputy Secretary of State Stephen Biegun discusses how a Democratic-controlled Congress could bring greater scrutiny to President Donald Trump’s foreign policy as the US renews efforts to negotiate an end to Russia’s war in Ukraine. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Wall Street Races for Megadeals as Countdown Begins on Trump Era
item.description: President Donald Trump’s return to the White House changed the political calculus around mergers and acquisitions, reviving companies’ desire for dream deals that had become difficult to pull off. Now, corporate America is on the clock.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Gould

item.title: Democratic Sweep Tests Trump-Linked Trades Across Latin America
item.description: Investors who spent the past year factoring countries’ standing with Donald Trump into their Latin America trades are confronting a new variable: a Democratic-controlled US Congress.
item.dc:creator: Vinícius Andrade, Carolina Wilson and Nicolle Yapur

item.title: How Everyday Apps Feed Police Surveillance
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg investigative journalist Ryan Gallagher explains how location data collected through everyday smartphone apps can ultimately be sold to law enforcement agencies, often without users knowing where their information ends up. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Gallagher details how Penlink’s surveillance technology can track phones using commercially obtained data and why its use has fueled calls for greater privacy protections and oversight. (Source: Bloomberg)
